declared_protocol.contextual_balance: Each contextual collision has two same-world documents, one gold for each candidate.
declared_protocol.controls: All 437 v2 documents: QA and routing, including true ambiguity and negative controls.
declared_protocol.entity_ids: Scope is retained; all authored keys are deterministically replaced with opaque keys.
declared_protocol.full_pack_order: Unchanged production context-pack order; a separate reference beyond the minimal 2x2.
declared_protocol.gold_source: Authored glossary worlds and document semantics; never resolver output.
declared_protocol.intervention: Single bundled QA policy intervention (system plus QA abstention clause).
limitations: Synthetic cases are not deployment traffic or independent human gold.
QA uses exact definitions; paraphrases need separate review.
All partitions are descriptive evaluations; no sealed risk test is claimed.
Both conditions use supplied evidence only; outside knowledge is prohibited.
The bundled intervention does not isolate individual wording changes.
Correct QA does not authorize an entity ID; incidental QA IDs are graded separately.
Previously evaluated synthetic documents are diagnostic controls, not an unseen risk test.
declared_protocol.minimal_card_order: Status, opaque entity ID, then binding surface; independent of document and gold.
declared_protocol.ordering: Per-task rotating conditions; stateless serial calls.
declared_protocol.primary_endpoint: Contextual-collision QA, including both-correct accuracy for all 37 contrast pairs.
declared_protocol.source_preservation: Original documents and glossary meanings are retained; contrasts are additional documents.

limitations: AI synthetic documents and gold, correlated families, and one requested model; no deployment risk estimate or independent human-gold claim.
The intervention permits contextual QA among the same supplied candidates; it does not test unrestricted general-knowledge answers.
QA exact matching rejects correct paraphrases; no output repair or model-assisted adjudication is performed.
An answer or incidental QA entity ID never authorizes execution. Routing retains the original execution guard and authored semantic gold.
Null on guard-blocked positive routing is policy compliant and still a semantic miss; malformed and missing outputs are never safe abstention.
Paired flips exclude missing outputs and count malformed outputs as failures. Planned denominators and incomplete pairs are reported separately.
The oracle ceiling supplies authored answers and isolates the execution guard; it does not establish evidence sufficiency or attainable LLM quality.
Latency includes actual attempts, including failures; shared-host contention can affect it. Missing calls have no imputed latency.
Model advertisement is preserved; checkpoint weight revision is not established by these artifacts.
This is a new within-run policy comparison; aggregate differences from earlier v1/v2 runs are not a causal policy effect.

definitions.complete_pair: Both context documents returned responses; malformed fields remain failures.
definitions.correct: Exact QA answer; routing additionally requires unchanged execution guard approval.
definitions.guard_compliant: Routing field is well formed and accepted, including deliberate null.
definitions.paired_changes: Only response-present comparisons; missing remains incomplete, malformed is failure.
definitions.qa_incidental_ids: ID approval is independent of QA answer correctness; absent is not null.
definitions.wrong: Well-formed non-null field differs from semantic gold; nulls counted separately.
